## [0.50.0] - 2026-11-10

Read before updating: Stop now ends a run at once, cutting off a teardown script's network calls; only one load or collection run can be live at a time; Vayu no longer replaces an engine that serves another data directory; and Settings now refuses proxy bypass entries, proxy passwords and pasted CA blocks that never worked (all under Changed). New: a send can be cancelled, streaming load runs show their events live and time the first event, Vayu names each cookie it drops, and the Dock shows an engine crash with a Restart button.

### Added

- **A send can be cancelled.** While a request is sending, **Cancel** sits beside the Send button. The request stops at the engine too, History records it as stopped, and variable writes its scripts made before the cancel are kept (#3379, #3391).
- **Streaming load runs show their events live.** A **Stream events** card shows events so far, events per second and streams open while the run goes, for a single request and for a collection load run with a streaming step. The dashboard used to stay blank until the streams ended (#3297, #3310).
- **Time to first event for streaming load runs.** First byte ends at the response headers, so a gateway that answered at once and then thought read as fast. The Stream events card and the report now have a first event row (p50, p95, p99, max), and two budgets go with it: **Time to first event p95 at most** and **Events per second at least** (#3294).
- The Markdown and HTML report exports have a Stream section, as the JSON export already did (#3298).
- **Vayu says when it drops a cookie.** A cookie over the size limit, past the 150 a request can carry or past the 50 a response can set was dropped with no word. A warning above the response now names each one, in a plain send, a streaming send and a collection run's step. A collection load run reports a count (#3314, #3317).
- **The Dock shows an engine crash.** The status tooltip names the cause ("Vayu's engine was stopped by signal 9.") and a **Restart** button sits beside it. The light used to stay on connected (#3372).
- An authorization-code sign-in can be cancelled from the OAuth 2.0 token row with **Cancel sign-in**, and one left unfinished times out after 5 minutes and frees its port (#3369, #3387).
- A collection run's step and a collection load run's **Steps** tab show how many variables did not resolve, beside the extractor misses (#3292).
- **A collection run reports HTTP/2 fallback.** The run header shows **HTTP/2 not negotiated** with a count, and the step says "HTTP/1.1, not HTTP/2", as single sends and load runs already did. Runs saved before this update still read 0 (#3284).
- **Settings > Client certificates** marks an entry Vayu cannot use (its file moved, for example) as **Not presented**, with the reason. It used to look healthy and was skipped on every send (#3318).
- The variables editor's conflict banner has **Keep mine** beside **Take theirs** (#3396).
- A failed update download says "Couldn't download Vayu X" with the reason and **Retry**. The progress bar used to stick (#3374).
- Settings > Keyboard shortcuts lists the window shortcuts (zoom, full screen, close window, quit) and the collection tree and tab strip ones (rename, delete, close tab), and a search for "zoom" finds them (#3394).

### Changed

- **Stop ends a run at once.** A Stop, or quitting Vayu, used to wait for whatever was in flight: a collection run's current step, a script's `pm.sendRequest`, a token request or renewal, a monitor scrape. Each is now cut off, so a teardown script's network cleanup does not happen on a stopped run, and its card reads "Skipped". A step cut short by Stop shows as stopped, is kept out of failures and latency, and the completion toast counts it (#3370, #3399, #3412).
- A Stop that arrives after a load run has finished keeps the run's own result (Completed, or Failed on a budget), and the dashboard says "The run had already finished when Stop arrived." A Stop during the run's last seconds no longer waits out the drain (#3365, #3411).
- **One live run at a time.** A load run, or a collection run from the Run Collection dialog, cannot start while another is live. The dialog says so, with **View run** and **Stop**. The second run used to take the dashboard while the first kept sending unseen. A run an agent starts meanwhile goes to the background, with a toast saying it will be in History (#3378, #3413).
- **Opening the app replaces only an engine that serves its own data directory.** A standalone `vayu-engine` with another `--data-dir`, or a second profile's engine, is left running, and the app moves to the next port. If every port is taken it says "Another Vayu engine is using port 9876. Quit it and press Retry." An engine left over from 0.49.0 or earlier is not replaced either: quit it by hand (#3384).
- **Settings refuses a Proxy bypass list entry that never matched**, such as `localhost:8080` or `*.example.com`, and names it. The host used to go through the proxy anyway. Accepted forms are an exact host, `.domain`, an IP, a range such as `10.0.0.0/8`, or `*` alone. A bad entry already stored is skipped and the rest still apply (#3283).
- A raw `@` in the proxy password is refused. Every send failed with `PROXY_ERROR` "Bad hostname"; write it as `%40` (#3283).
- **A pasted CA block that does not parse is refused**, naming which one ("certificate 2 of 3 does not parse"). Every `https://` send used to fail, public sites included. A bad block already stored is now left out (#3280).
- A variable name that is blank or starts or ends with a space is refused, since `{{ name }}` could never reach it. The variables editor trims names on save, and Postman and Insomnia imports trim names and skip blank ones (#3268).
- A down proxy is now `PROXY_ERROR` rather than `CONNECTION_FAILED`, and a forwarding proxy's 407 on an `http://` request is `PROXY_ERROR` rather than the server's response (#3282).
- An `http://` server that answers in another protocol, usually HTTP/2 without TLS, is reported as "The server answered in another protocol" with a tip to use `https://`, under `PROTOCOL_MISMATCH` rather than `INVALID_URL` (#3312).
- A cookie set during a redirect goes to the next hop only when scheme, host and port all match. It used to follow a port change and reach sibling domains through `Domain=` (#3309, #3311, #3313).
- A conflicted variable is not saved until you choose **Keep mine** or **Take theirs**; saving used to keep yours without asking. A failed variables save retries on its own (#3396).
- The settings connection test shows the proxy without its user and password, and says when the environment's proxy (`http_proxy`, `https_proxy`) carried the request. The MCP connection check never returns proxy credentials, even with **Reveal secrets to agents** on (#3291).
- Ctrl+Q quits on Windows (#3394).
- MCP `stop_run` on a streamed request answers the status History records, and `running` if the run has not settled (#3405).
- A variable stored through the API or MCP as a number, boolean or object is sent as that text. It went out empty, and the Postman export wrote `[object Object]` (#3286).
- A Postman environment export counts a secret typed number or boolean among the variable types left out (#3295).
- The **Export as OpenAPI** hint for **Values only** says operations no request claims are removed (#3277).
- For people driving the engine API: a raw `POST /runs` naming an environment or collection resolves `{{variables}}` from them, including in basic-auth credentials and response checks; blank environment and collection names are refused; a collection run with a top-level `stream` is refused; and updating a collection can only unbind its spec (#3287, #3293, #3299, #3368).
- Electron 44.10.0. On Linux X11, paste no longer hangs until restart (#3278).
- Internal: the MCP server, engine lifecycle, save status and shutdown were reworked, and tests and documentation kept in step.

### Fixed

- **A collection run sends a request saved with Event stream on as a stream.** It went out as an ordinary request, so it hit its timeout or "succeeded" with its events counted nowhere. The Run dialog shows the stream caps and budgets when a request in it streams (#3299).
- **A redirect to a host that needs a client certificate presents it.** Redirected from `http://` to an mTLS `https://` host, a request failed with "certificate required". Fixed for plain sends, streams and load runs (#3309, #3311, #3313).
- **An OAuth 2.0 refresh no longer signs you out.** Two sends that found a token expired both refreshed it, and with a provider that rotates refresh tokens Vayu then deleted the token the first had saved. A 503 or 429 during a refresh also deleted it. Only the provider rejecting the refresh token clears it now (#3359, #3364).
- **With Event stream on, a reply that was not an event stream kept its body.** A 401 or 429 from an LLM API showed "No events received" and an empty Body. The Events tab now names the type the server sent and points to Body, and scripts can read it. A finished stream shows the bytes received instead of `0 B` (#3272).
- **In a collection run with sub-folders, each step uses its own folder's variables.** Once a script or extractor wrote a variable, a sub-folder's `{{var}}` went out with its braces, and `pm.collectionVariables` used the run's collection (#3266).
- A secret variable on a sub-folder was stored in clear in the run's saved snapshot (#3275).
- A teardown script's `pm.environment.set` and `pm.globals.set` were dropped (#3273).
- After a collection run, the Variables pane and `{{variable}}` previews kept the old values while the next Send used the new ones (#3267).
- Switching tabs during a send re-enabled Send, so the request could go out twice and the slower answer won. A streamed request that finished in another tab showed an older run when you came back (#3379, #3393).
- A run stopped while starting could be recorded as completed, and a run's duration included its cleanup, so RPS read slightly low. A load run's report read mid-run showed rates far too high (#3362).
- In a load run, a stream cut off mid-reply counted as an internal error rather than a connection failure, and a stream with no events counted as one event (#3298).
- A quiet stream ends within a couple of seconds of **Stream idle timeout** (#3296).
- A capped stream stored one extra, half-received event, and an event of exactly the size limit was flagged as truncated (#3264).
- In the variables editor, renaming a variable onto a name in use, or clearing its name, deleted a variable. The row now stays with "Name already used" or "Needs a name" (#3268).
- Two quick variable saves landing out of order could hide an agent's change or show a false conflict, and a save for a deleted environment left the Dock on "Saving…" (#3396).
- The Dock lost track of saves: a tab switch cleared "Not saved" on an unsaved variables edit, and a failed save on quit left "Unsaved changes" up for good (#3373).
- After a failed save on quit, **Keep working** left the next quit with no save and no warning (#3358).
- **Close other tabs** and **Close tabs to the right** keep unsaved tabs while the engine is unreachable (#3330).
- Cancelling a save dialog still showed "Exported". The toast now waits for the file, and a failed write names the reason (#3289, #3290).
- An exported run report listed each unresolved variable twice, and its baseline comparison called a changed request count unchanged (#3289).
- The Tests and Console panes of a finished streaming request could stay empty until reopened (#3285).
- The OAuth 2.0 token row and the load test dialog said "No token cached" while still checking, and the row could show a green dot next to "expired 10s ago" (#3387, #3390).
- Opening the dashboard as a run ended announced it as stopped (#3386).
- Previewing an HTML response during a load test turned off **Keep the machine awake during runs** and the taskbar progress (#3389).
- Switching environments quickly could leave every send on an environment the engine had refused (#3385).
- Two overlapping engine restarts could each start an engine, and a restart during startup quit the app (#3372).
- Turning **Enable MCP server** off while it was starting left it listening (#3375).
- "Ready to install" was lost when the window reloaded (#3374).
- A file or link opened through the OS while the window reloaded was lost, and **New Request** from the Dock or Jump List did nothing while a dialog was open (#3376, #3409).
- An environment in the Trash no longer lists its cookies, and **Delete forever** removes them (#3366).
- `pm.cookies` left out a Secure cookie on `localhost` over `http://`, though the request carried it (#3279).
- An imported environment keeps the file's variable order (#3295).
- An `http://` send no longer shows the mTLS chip (#3318).
- A send from a History run's editable copy was recorded as "Untitled request" (#3356).
- Ctrl/Cmd+N focuses the URL field (#3406).
- On Windows and Linux, Alt+scroll opened the application menu (#3408).
- Ctrl/Cmd+K no longer opens the command palette over another dialog, where its commands acted underneath (#3329).
- Command palette: Enter on a search with no matches no longer opens a blank request; tab rows name their collection; a pasted `{{baseUrl}}` finds the variable; Settings rows no longer match on stray letters; Save shows only on tabs that save; and closing a tab moves focus to the next one (#3357, #3392, #3395, #3407, #3410).
- Postman export, as Newman runs it: a query written only in the URL was left out, a JSON-RPC body lacked `jsonrpc` and `id`, and a typed `Authorization` header was overwritten by the request's auth (#3265, #3271, #3274).
